chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother al-Hasan, from Zur'a ibn Muhammad, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) paused at Mina when he completed his rituals during the Farewell Hajj. He said: 'O people! Listen to what I say to you, and understand it from me, for I do not know — perhaps I will not meet you in this standing place after this year of ours.'

Then he said: 'Which day is the greatest in sanctity?' They said, 'This day.' He said: 'So which month is the greatest in sanctity?' They said, 'This month.' He said: 'And which land is the greatest in sanctity?' They said, 'This land.' He said: 'Indeed, your blood and your wealth are forbidden to you, like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this land of yours, until the day you meet Him and He questions you about your deeds.'

Behold, have I delivered (the message)?' They said, 'Yes.' He said: 'O God, bear witness! Verily, whoever has a trust with him, let him return it to the one who entrusted it to him. For the blood of a Muslim person is not permissible, nor his wealth, except with his own consent. Do not be unjust to yourselves, and do not return to being disbelievers after me.'

key_terms.أمانة: Trust, entrustment — anything held in trust for another, including property, secrets, and responsibilities
key_terms.بطيبة نفسه: By the willingness/pleasure of his soul — indicates that only genuinely free and willing consent can make another's property permissible
key_terms.حجة الوداع: The Farewell Hajj — the Prophet's final pilgrimage in year 10 AH, approximately 3 months before his death
key_terms.حرمة: Sanctity, inviolability, sacred status — the quality that makes something forbidden to violate

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say during the Farewell Hajj about the sanctity of Muslim blood and wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrating the Prophet Muhammad's (SAWW) final sermon at Mina during the Farewell Hajj (10 AH / 632 CE). Addressing approximately 100,000 pilgrims, the Prophet used a rhetorical method of sacred analogy — asking about the most sacred day (the Day of 'Arafat), month (Dhul-Hijja), and city (Mecca) — to establish that Muslim life, blood, and wealth carry equivalent and permanent sanctity. The three core injunctions — honoring trusts (amanah), prohibiting the taking of life and wealth without consent, and warning against apostasy — were understood by the original audience as foundational principles of the new Islamic social order.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from his brother Al Hassan, from Zur’at Bin Muhammad, from Sama’at,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said that Rasool-Allah<sup>azwj</sup> paused at Mina where he fulfilled his<sup>saww</sup>rituals during the farewell Hajj. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O you people!, Listen to what I<sup>saww</sup> am saying to you all, therefore understand from me<sup>saww</sup>, for I<sup>saww</sup> do not know perhaps I<sup>saww</sup> will not meet you all in this pausing place after this year of ours’.

Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Which day is greatest in sanctity?’ They said, ‘This day’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So which month is the greatest in sanctity?’ They said, ‘This month’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Which city is greatest in sanctity?’ They said, ‘This city’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So your blood and your wealth is sacred upon you all like the sacredness of this days of yours, in this month of yours, in this city of yours, up to the Day you meet Him<sup>azwj</sup>, so He<sup>azwj</sup> would be Questioning you all about your deeds.

Indeed! Have I<sup>saww</sup> delivered (the Message)?’ They said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Be Witness! Indeed, and the one with whom was deposited an entrustment, so let him pay it back to the one who had entrusted it upon him, for neither the blood of a Muslim person nor his wealth is Permissible except by him agreeing it himself, and do not be unjust to yourselves (commit sins), nor return to be disbelievers after me<sup>saww</sup>’.
